content: Politico is reporting that members of the Trump administration asked Ohio Republicans not to wage a public pressure campaign against the embattled representative Max Miller despite allegations of domestic abuse against him. The move comes as Miller has decided to stay in the race despite mounting calls for his resignation, refusing to step aside as the Republican nominee for Ohio’s 7th Congressional District ahead of Monday afternoon’s deadline. Trump administration officials argued that messaging would get complicated if the same leaders who called for Miller’s resignation would later have to defend him in the general election. “They basically told us to back off,” an Ohio Republican involved in the conversations told Politico, “and let the voters decide.” Donald Trump’s administration is facing questions over whether it is using Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to “surveil political opponents” after an investigative agent was apparently stationed outside Democratic representative Ilhan Omar’s monthly town hall meeting in Richfield, Minnesota. After the incident, Omar demanded the US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) clarify whether Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) agents have been used to monitor “any other activity” involving “local, state, or federal officials” in the state. In a letter to Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), an arm of ICE, the congresswoman said an agent claiming to be conducting an undercover drug operation was parked outside the community center where she was holding an event last Thursday, without prior coordination with local law enforcement. According to Omar, who represents Minnesota’s fifth congressional district, a Richfield police officer noticed the agent sitting in a Ford Explorer and “became suspicious of the way she was monitoring the building”. Read the full story here: Republican senator Bill Cassidy, a trained physician, called Trump’s latest executive order spacing out childhood vaccines “wrong.” “I’m a doctor. This executive order is wrong,” he said in a post on social media. “The President does not have the expertise to make these changes.” “Vaccines are overwhelmingly safe. Vaccines are effective. Vaccines DO NOT cause autism,” Cassidy added. “Breaking up vaccines will mean children have to get more shots to get the same protection, not fewer shots. It will increase hesitancy and make children less safe.” “Parents should listen to their child’s pediatrician about vaccines rather than listening to an inaccurate executive order. This is so wrong,” he wrote on Monday. A judge has temporarily blocked New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax, which would place a surcharge on second homes in the city, the Wall Street Journal reports. The emergency pause comes after a group of homeowners filed a lawsuit against Mamdani and the city’s finance director over the tax last week. They allege the city wrongly identified their homes as potentially subject to the surcharge despite the properties serving as their primary residences. “The city has arbitrarily and capriciously foisted onto New York City residents the burden of proving they are not subject to the surcharge,” reads the complaint filed on Friday. Amid the judge’s order on Monday, the city is barred from issuing any additional notices. Mamdani’s critics accuse the democratic socialist mayor of targeting the wealthy, while others have welcomed the tax, seeing it as a helpful way to raise revenue from affluent property owners in a city grappling with a high cost of living. Also asking Max Miller to step aside are members of the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, one of whom called the allegations against the congressmember “horrific” and “credible.” “The horrific allegations levied against Max Miller, who has a lengthy record of alleged domestic violence, are credible and cannot be ignored,” said DCCC spokesperson Riya Vashi. “Rather than step aside, Miller has chosen to cling to power and put his family and his constituents through a public spectacle of his own making,” Vashi added. “Let’s be clear: this is the same playbook Max Miller has run before — deny, deflect, and drag his accusers through the mud.” The Trump administration has extended for 90 days ⁠a waiver allowing foreign-flagged ships carrying oil and gas to travel between US ports, White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said in a post on social media. The waiver extension, which will take effect on 17 August, applies to the Jones Act, a law passed in 1920 that requires shipping between ports in the US to be conducted under US ships. Rogers said the extension was granted to “ensure our military and key industries maintain uninterrupted access to critical resources”. “Data shows the waiver has driven a significant increase in domestic deliveries of essential products such as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel,” Rogers wrote. New limits were imposed after shipbuilders and members in Congress argued the policy was undermining the domestic maritime ⁠industry. Now, the waiver will only apply to cargo that are sources of energy and commodities related to agriculture, per the AP. The waiver comes as the strait of Hormuz, a primary waterway for shipping oil and natural gas, remains effectively closed because of the war. chineseContent: 据《Politico》报道，特朗普政府成员要求俄亥俄州共和党人不要对陷入困境的众议员马克斯·米勒(Max Miller)发起公众压力运动，尽管他受到家庭虐待的指控。此举发生之际，尽管要求他辞职的呼声越来越高，米勒仍决定继续参加竞选，并拒绝在周一下午的截止日期前辞去俄亥俄州第七国会选区共和党候选人的职务。特朗普政府官员认为，如果呼吁米勒辞职的领导人后来不得不在大选中为他辩护，那么传递的信息就会变得复杂。一位参与对话的俄亥俄州共和党人告诉 Politico，“他们基本上是让我们退后一步，让选民来决定。”一名调查人员显然驻扎在民主党代表伊尔汗·奥马尔在明尼苏达州里奇菲尔德举行的每月市政厅会议外，唐纳德·特朗普政府正面临是否使用移民和海关执法局（ICE）“监视政治对手”的质疑。事件发生后，奥马尔要求美国国土安全部（DHS）澄清国土安全调查（HSI）特工是否被用来监视该州涉及“地方、州或联邦官员”的“任何其他活动”。这位女议员在给 ICE 下属国土安全调查局 (HSI) 的一封信中表示，一名自称正在进行卧底毒品行动的特工将车停在她上周四举办活动的社区中心外，而事先没有与当地执法部门协调。代表明尼苏达州第五国会选区的奥马尔表示，一名里奇菲尔德警官注意到这名特工坐在一辆福特探险者中，并“对他的行为方式产生了怀疑”。
